summary: arXiv:2611.23254v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For more than seventy years, systems engineering has developed extensive models and frameworks, yet the fundamental question of what constitutes a system remains insufficiently formalized. Existing approaches often treat structure and behavior as separate aspects, leaving their unity, system identity, and consistency conditions insufficiently defined. This paper introduces Structure-Behavior Coalescence (SBC) as a formal framework that defines a system as an integrated entity in which structure and behavior are coalesced through interaction. SBC provides a formal modeling approach with well-formedness constraints for maintaining structural-behavioral coherence, including representations for terminal, paused, and intermediate states and rules for sequential, parallel, and alternative behaviors. The framework provides a formal perspective on the question, "What is a system?", and establishes a foundation for consistent system modeling, verification, and analysis.
title: Structure-Behavior Coalescence: A Definition of Systems
